messages.author: 6f70bde37a2bc2fe
messages.subject: SPDE prediction without inla.stack()
parts:
First off, thanks to the developers for all the work building R-INLA. I've found it to be really useful in my work. I am pretty new to this approach so forgive me if my question comes off as misinformed.

I'm trying to build a spatial model using grouped data (100+ groups) and would like to generate a prediction for any of the groups. From what I understand, I could create 100+ prediction stacks and combine them with the estimation stack and pass that to inla() as the data object. This seems expensive and I was wondering if it's possible to estimate the model using just the estimation stack, and run prediction after the model object is created? Any comments/guidance would be much appreciated, thanks!

Brian


Loc <- cbind(df$X, df$Y)
loc.domain <- expand.grid(-15:15, 15:45)
Mesh1 <- inla.mesh.2d(loc.domain=loc.domain, cutoff=6,
                      offset=c(6,9),
                      max.edge = c(6, 9))

A_point <- inla.spde.make.A(Mesh1, loc=Loc,
                            group=groups,
                            group.mesh=inla.mesh.1d(groups, degree=0),
                            n.group=n_groups)

spde1 <- inla.spde2.matern(Mesh1, alpha = 2, constr=TRUE)

s.index <- inla.spde.make.index(name="spatial.field1",
                                n.spde=spde1$n.spde,
                                n.group=n_groups)

stack.est <- inla.stack(data=list(y=df$response),
                        A=list(A_point),
                        effects=list(c(s.index,
                                       list(intercept=1)
                        )
                        ), tag="est")

formula_p1 <- y ~ -1 + intercept +
  f(spatial.field1, model = spde1, group=spatial.field1.group,
    control.group=list(model='rw1', scale.model=TRUE)
  )
######
# I could create 100+ of these and combine them with stack.est into join.stack
######
group_1 <- 1
A_pred <- inla.spde.make.A(Mesh1, loc=as.matrix(pred.grid),
                           group=rep(group_1, nrow(pred.grid)),
                           n.group=n_groups)


stack.pred.response <- inla.stack(data=list(y=NA),
                                  A=list(A_pred),
                                  effects=list(c(s.index, list(intercept=1))), tag="pred")

join.stack <- inla.stack(stack.est, stack.pred.response)

join.output.1 <- inla(formula_p1, data=inla.stack.data(join.stack), family='binomial', Ntrials=1,
                    control.family=list(link='logit'),
                    control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(join.stack), compute=TRUE, link=c(1)),
                    control.compute = list(dic = TRUE),
                    verbose=TRUE
)

######
# Can I create just the estimated model and run prediction after?
######

join.output.2 <- inla(formula_p1, data=inla.stack.data(stack.est), family='binomial', Ntrials=1,
                    control.family=list(link='logit'),
                    control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack.est), compute=TRUE, link=c(1)),
                    control.compute = list(dic = TRUE),
                    verbose=TRUE
)

# Predict group 1 over A_pred using join.output.2?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: SPDE prediction without inla.stack()
parts:
Hi,
That sentence should be rewritten!

For this kind of situation, one can use inla.posterior.sample() to sample from the model components, which then allows computing any type of prediction via Monte Carlo estimates (averages of the samples for expectations and variances, and quantiles for posterior quantiles, etc). The sampling method produces independent posterior samples  (so it is not comparable to slow MCMC).

The inlabru package does have a predict() function that encapsulates this type of procedure. (The current CRAN version has some practical limitations of what type of inla models are supported, but an upcoming update Will have more complete and consistent support.)

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: SPDE prediction without inla.stack()
parts:
Thanks Finn,

Searching through the archives of this forum I've found some examples where inla.posterior.sample() is used to make prediction, but it's not clear how to incorporate the group into the prediction. My understanding is inla.posterior.sample() could be used to get samples of intercept and spatial.field1 (in my code example) corresponding to locations observed in the projector matrix A_point, but I haven't been able to figure out how to sample from spatial.field1 for a specific group. Is this possible?


# Run prediction without stack
n=10
samples = inla.posterior.sample(n=n,fit)
contents=fit$misc$configs$contents

## intercept
idx_intercept=which(contents$tag=="intercept")
idx_intercept=contents$start[idx_intercept]:(contents$start[idx_intercept]+contents$length[idx_intercept]-1)
intercept = lapply(samples, function(x) x$latent[idx_intercept])
intercept = matrix(unlist(intercept), ncol = length(idx_intercept), byrow = T)

## spatial.field1
idx_spat=which(contents$tag=="spatial.field1")
idx_spat=contents$start[idx_spat]:(contents$start[idx_spat]+contents$length[idx_spat]-1)
spat = lapply(samples, function(x) x$latent[idx_spat])
spat = matrix(unlist(spat), ncol = length(idx_spat), byrow = T)

### Predict over observed locations in "est" stack - not sure how to incorporate group
pred_idx = inla.stack.index(stack.est,tag="est")$data
by_inla_post = t(intercept) + spat[,pred_idx]

Thanks Finn,
Yes, does what I'm doing in the following code below make sense?

I seem to get point predictions corresponding to the X/Y locations in Mesh1$loc, but they seem off - I would like to confirm that I've aligned the locations with the predictions correctly, or maybe it's something else?

Another question: is it possible to use this method to make predictions at X/Y locations not in Mesh$loc?

# Run prediction without stack
n=10
samples = inla.posterior.sample(n=n,fit)
contents=fit$misc$configs$contents

## intercept
idx_intercept=which(contents$tag=="intercept")
idx_intercept=contents$start[idx_intercept]:(contents$start[idx_intercept]+contents$length[idx_intercept]-1)
intercept = lapply(samples, function(x) x$latent[idx_intercept])
intercept = matrix(unlist(intercept), ncol = length(idx_intercept), byrow = T)

## spatial.field1
idx_spat=which(contents$tag=="spatial.field1")
idx_spat=contents$start[idx_spat]:(contents$start[idx_spat]+contents$length[idx_spat]-1)
spat = lapply(samples, function(x) x$latent[idx_spat])
spat = matrix(unlist(spat), ncol = length(idx_spat), byrow = T)

pred_grid <- Mesh1$loc
grid_length <- nrow(Mesh1$loc)
# Choose a group to predict with
group_index <- 20
group_spatial_index <- (grid_length * (group_index-1) + 1):(grid_length * group_index)

# Predict using 1 sample from the posterior
pred <- intercept[1] + spat[1,group_spatial_index]
pred <- exp(pred)/(1+exp(pred))

# Combine Mesh1$loc with prediction - are these two objects aligned correctly?
data <- cbind(data.frame(pred_grid[,1:2]), pred)

On Thu, 25 Jun 2020, 18:13 S. Brian Huey, <sbh...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks Finn,

Searching through the archives of this forum I've found some examples where inla.posterior.sample() is used to make prediction, but it's not clear how to incorporate the group into the prediction. My understanding is inla.posterior.sample() could be used to get samples of intercept and spatial.field1 (in my code example) corresponding to locations observed in the projector matrix A_point, but I haven't been able to figure out how to sample from spatial.field1 for a specific group. Is this possible?


# Run prediction without stack
n=10
samples = inla.posterior.sample(n=n,fit)
contents=fit$misc$configs$contents

## intercept
idx_intercept=which(contents$tag=="intercept")
idx_intercept=contents$start[idx_intercept]:(contents$start[idx_intercept]+contents$length[idx_intercept]-1)
intercept = lapply(samples, function(x) x$latent[idx_intercept])
intercept = matrix(unlist(intercept), ncol = length(idx_intercept), byrow = T)

## spatial.field1
idx_spat=which(contents$tag=="spatial.field1")
idx_spat=contents$start[idx_spat]:(contents$start[idx_spat]+contents$length[idx_spat]-1)
spat = lapply(samples, function(x) x$latent[idx_spat])
spat = matrix(unlist(spat), ncol = length(idx_spat), byrow = T)

### Predict over observed locations in "est" stack - not sure how to incorporate group
pred_idx = inla.stack.index(stack.est,tag="est")$data
by_inla_post = t(intercept) + spat[,pred_idx]


On Wednesday, June 24, 2020 at 11:51:49 PM UTC-7, Finn Lindgren wrote:

Hi,
That sentence should be rewritten!

For this kind of situation, one can use inla.posterior.sample() to sample from the model components, which then allows computing any type of prediction via Monte Carlo estimates (averages of the samples for expectations and variances, and quantiles for posterior quantiles, etc). The sampling method produces independent posterior samples  (so it is not comparable to slow MCMC).

The inlabru package does have a predict() function that encapsulates this type of procedure. (The current CRAN version has some practical limitations of what type of inla models are supported, but an upcoming update Will have more complete and consistent support.)

Finn

On 25 Jun 2020, at 06:06, Mark <mille...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿
Hi,

From the INLA website: "In INLA there is  no function ``predict'' as for glm/lm in R. Predictions must to done as a part of the model fitting itself."

Hope this helps,

Mark



On Thursday, June 25, 2020 at 12:40:40 AM UTC-4, S. Brian Huey wrote:
First off, thanks to the developers for all the work building R-INLA. I've found it to be really useful in my work. I am pretty new to this approach so forgive me if my question comes off as misinformed.

I'm trying to build a spatial model using grouped data (100+ groups) and would like to generate a prediction for any of the groups. From what I understand, I could create 100+ prediction stacks and combine them with the estimation stack and pass that to inla() as the data object. This seems expensive and I was wondering if it's possible to estimate the model using just the estimation stack, and run prediction after the model object is created? Any comments/guidance would be much appreciated, thanks!

Brian


Loc <- cbind(df$X, df$Y)
loc.domain <- expand.grid(-15:15, 15:45)
Mesh1 <- inla.mesh.2d(loc.domain=loc.domain, cutoff=6,
                      offset=c(6,9),
                      max.edge = c(6, 9))

A_point <- inla.spde.make.A(Mesh1, loc=Loc,
                            group=groups,
                            group.mesh=inla.mesh.1d(groups, degree=0),
                            n.group=n_groups)

spde1 <- inla.spde2.matern(Mesh1, alpha = 2, constr=TRUE)

s.index <- inla.spde.make.index(name="spatial.field1",
                                n.spde=spde1$n.spde,
                                n.group=n_groups)

stack.est <- inla.stack(data=list(y=df$response),
                        A=list(A_point),
                        effects=list(c(s.index,
                                       list(intercept=1)
                        )
                        ), tag="est")

formula_p1 <- y ~ -1 + intercept +
  f(spatial.field1, model = spde1, group=spatial.field1.group,
    control.group=list(model='rw1', scale.model=TRUE)
  )
######
# I could create 100+ of these and combine them with stack.est into join.stack
######
group_1 <- 1
A_pred <- inla.spde.make.A(Mesh1, loc=as.matrix(pred.grid),
                           group=rep(group_1, nrow(pred.grid)),
                           n.group=n_groups)


stack.pred.response <- inla.stack(data=list(y=NA),
                                  A=list(A_pred),
                                  effects=list(c(s.index, list(intercept=1))), tag="pred")

join.stack <- inla.stack(stack.est, stack.pred.response)

join.output.1 <- inla(formula_p1, data=inla.stack.data(join.stack), family='binomial', Ntrials=1,
                    control.family=list(link='logit'),
                    control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(join.stack), compute=TRUE, link=c(1)),
                    control.compute = list(dic = TRUE),
                    verbose=TRUE
)

######
# Can I create just the estimated model and run prediction after?
######

join.output.2 <- inla(formula_p1, data=inla.stack.data(stack.est), family='binomial', Ntrials=1,
                    control.family=list(link='logit'),
                    control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack.est), compute=TRUE, link=c(1)),
                    control.compute = list(dic = TRUE),
                    verbose=TRUE
)

# Predict group 1 over A_pred using join.output.2?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: SPDE prediction without inla.stack()
parts:
Hi,

I would extract the entire model component that includes _all_ the
groups for the field; it's one single latent component, full_field.
Then call inla.spde.make.A with the mesh, and the desired loc and
group combinations;
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=prediction_locations, group=prediction_group)
Then A%*%full_field should be the evaluated field for each row of
cbind(prediction_locations, prediction_group)

I try to avoid the direct indexing as much as possible, and use the
available wrapper functions like inla.spde.make.A to do the work for
me.

Finn
